task_signatures.pattern: BUD for single-dose container after puncture
task_signatures.correct_strategy: Identify container type (single-dose) and environment (sterile vs non-sterile), then apply the USP <797> single-dose BUD rule for the stated environment
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Applying multi-dose vial rules to a single-dose container, or ignoring the environmental condition

task_signatures.pattern: BUD for multi-dose vial after first puncture
task_signatures.correct_strategy: Apply USP <797> multi-dose vial in-use period; check if manufacturer specifies a shorter period and use the more conservative value
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Using the manufacturer expiration date instead of the in-use BUD

task_signatures.correct_strategy: Classify the CSP by category (immediate use, Category 1, Category 2), then apply the corresponding BUD based on storage condition
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Applying a single BUD rule to all CSPs regardless of category or storage condition

failure_modes: confusing_expiration_with_BUD: using manufacturer expiration date instead of the post-opening or post-compounding BUD
ignoring_environment: not distinguishing between sterile and non-sterile environment when determining BUD
wrong_container_rule: applying multi-dose rules to single-dose containers or vice versa
wrong_usp_chapter: applying USP <800> rules to a non-hazardous drug scenario
key_principles: BUD is always determined by container type × environment × USP chapter — all three must be identified
Single-dose containers have stricter BUD limits than multi-dose containers
When environment is unstated, default to the more conservative BUD
Expiration date and BUD are distinct concepts — never confuse them
